item: A signed key-rotation record lets the custody log verify across a change of key
summary: When the key that signs now did not sign the tail, the log writes a key-rotation record first, signed by the new key and saying in plain words that the previous key was not available. CustodyLog.rotate_signing_key writes an endorsed one: the old key signs the new key and the chain position. The checker follows an endorsed rotation and names it; refuses an unendorsed one unless accept_unendorsed_rotation (--accept-unendorsed-rotation) is passed; and refuses a key change with no record, so a forged tail stays refused. One-item exports carry the rotation records up to their last entry.
